chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt from Yunus said:

The fasting person in the month of Ramadan may use the siwak (tooth-stick) whenever he wishes. And if he rinses his mouth during the time of obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, there is no blame upon him and his fast is complete. But if he rinses his mouth during non-obligatory prayer time and water enters his throat, he must repeat the fast. The best for the fasting person is to not rinse his mouth.

And we have explained in the Chapter of the Sunnah of the Fasting Person what the fasting person must avoid from that which breaks the fast, so there is no need for repetition. And we will explain in the following chapter what of it requires making up (qada) and expiation (kaffarah), from the total of what we have mentioned previously, if God Almighty wills.
ai.seo_question: Does rinsing the mouth break the fast in Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between rinsing the mouth during obligatory prayer times (*waqt al-faridah*), where water entering the throat does not invalidate the fast, and during other times, where it does require *qada* (making up the fast). The text highlights the principle of *istihbab* (preference) for avoiding rinsing entirely to prevent doubt, while referencing prior discussions on acts that nullify the fast versus those that merely impair its conditions. This reflects the Shia scholarly focus on distinguishing between minor impurities that do not break the fast and those that do, based on the timing and intent of the action.
